newsitem.title: USA: GM Q2 Latin American sales rise 31.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: GM Q2 Latin American sales rise 31.7 pct.

text.p: General Motors Corp said Thursday that second quarter vehicle sales in Latin America were 164,000 units, a 31.7 percent increase and a new record for the quarter.
GM vehicle sales for the first half of 1997 were more than 300,000 units, the automaker said, 15.7 percent above 1996 results and also a new record.

"The vehicle industry throughout Latin America continues to expand strongly with significant consumer demand in Brazil and Argentina, as well as the long- awaited recovery in Venezuela, where the industry has improved by 165 percent compared to 1996," Ricahrd Nerod, group vice president for Latin America, Middle East and African operations said in a statement.

GM has been operating in Latin America since 1925. Capacity expansion programs previously announced include new vehicle assembly plants in Brazil and Argentina and modernization programs in the Andean region.
